description: This topic explains the meaning, evolution and functions of money, the qualities of good money, the problems of barter trade, the types and functions of banks, and the banking services that support trade.

mcq.questionText: What is the main reason money was introduced to replace barter trade?

options.text: To remove the need for a double coincidence of wants
To force everyone to use banks

mcq.explanation: Barter required both traders to want what the other offered at the same time. Money removed this difficulty by acting as a common medium of exchange.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best defines money?

options.text: Anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange
Only coins issued by the government
Goods exchanged directly for other goods
A written promise to deliver goods later

mcq.explanation: Money is anything generally accepted by people in a society as a means of paying for goods and services and settling debts.

mcq.questionText: Which one is NOT a function of money?
mcq.explanation: Money serves as a medium of exchange, a measure of value, a store of value and a standard of deferred payment, but it does not produce raw materials.

mcq.questionText: A good form of money should be divisible. What does divisibility mean?

options.text: It can be split into smaller units for small payments
It can be eaten when there is hunger
It is accepted only in one town

mcq.explanation: Divisibility means money can be broken into smaller units, for example shillings into cents, so that both large and small transactions can be made.

mcq.questionText: Which institution is responsible for issuing currency notes and coins in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The central bank, the Bank of Tanzania, has the sole authority to issue and control the supply of currency in the country.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a function of a commercial bank?

options.text: Accepting deposits and giving loans to the public
Acting as banker to the government only

mcq.explanation: Commercial banks accept deposits from the public and lend money to individuals and businesses, while currency issue and interest-rate control belong to the central bank.

mcq.questionText: Why is the central bank called the 'banker to the government'?

options.text: It keeps government accounts and handles its payments
It is owned by private traders
It sells goods to the government
It pays salaries to all citizens

mcq.explanation: The central bank keeps the government's accounts, receives its revenue and makes its payments, acting as banker and adviser to the government.

mcq.questionText: A cheque is best described as a:

options.text: Coin issued by the central bank
Written order to a bank to pay a stated sum from an account
Receipt for goods bought on credit

mcq.explanation: A cheque is a written order instructing a bank to pay a specified amount of money from the drawer's account to a named person or business.

mcq.questionText: Which type of bank account usually earns the highest interest and is meant for keeping money for a long period?
mcq.explanation: A fixed deposit account holds money for an agreed period during which it cannot be withdrawn, so it earns the highest rate of interest.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following was commonly used as a medium of exchange before modern money existed?
mcq.explanation: During the evolution of money, commodities such as cattle, salt and cowrie shells were used as early forms of money before coins and notes were introduced.

mcq.questionText: An overdraft facility allows a current account holder to:

options.text: Withdraw more money than is in the account up to an agreed limit

mcq.explanation: An overdraft lets a current account holder withdraw beyond the available balance up to an agreed limit, and interest is charged on the amount overdrawn.

mcq.questionText: Which quality of money refers to it not wearing out or rotting easily?
mcq.explanation: Durability means money lasts a long time and does not easily wear out, tear or decay, so it can be used repeatedly.

mcq.questionText: The central bank acts as a 'lender of last resort'. This means it:

options.text: Lends money to ordinary customers in shops
Lends money to commercial banks facing shortage of funds
Refuses to lend money to anyone
Gives free money to the public

mcq.explanation: As lender of last resort, the central bank provides funds to commercial banks that are short of money, helping to keep the banking system stable.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a way banking helps trade?

options.text: It makes payments safe and easy through cheques and transfers
It increases the cost of all goods
It stops traders from getting loans
It forces traders to carry large amounts of cash

mcq.explanation: Banks help trade by providing safe means of payment, safekeeping of money, loans and money transfer services, reducing the risks of carrying cash.

mcq.questionText: A savings account is most suitable for a person who wants to:

options.text: Make many daily payments by cheque
Keep small amounts safely and earn some interest

mcq.explanation: A savings account encourages people to save small amounts safely while earning a modest interest, with limited withdrawals.

fib.questionText: The direct exchange of goods for goods without using money is called _____.
fib.explanation: Barter trade is the system of exchanging one good or service directly for another without using money.

fib.questionText: A situation where two people each want exactly what the other has to offer at the same time is known as the double coincidence of _____.
fib.explanation: The double coincidence of wants was a major problem of barter trade because both parties had to want each other's goods.

fib.questionText: Anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange is called _____.
fib.explanation: Money is defined as anything generally accepted by society as a means of exchange and settlement of debts.

fib.questionText: The bank that has the sole right to issue currency in a country is the _____ bank.
fib.explanation: The central bank, the Bank of Tanzania, is the only body allowed to issue notes and coins in the country.

fib.questionText: A bank account from which money can be withdrawn at any time using cheques is called a _____ account.
fib.explanation: A current account allows frequent deposits and withdrawals and the use of cheques, but usually earns little or no interest.

fib.questionText: The quality of money that allows it to be carried easily from one place to another is called _____.
fib.explanation: Portability means money should be light and easy to carry so that it is convenient to use in trade.

fib.questionText: The person who writes and signs a cheque ordering the bank to pay is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The drawer is the account holder who writes and signs the cheque instructing the bank to make payment.

fib.questionText: Money kept and used today to buy goods in the future shows that money acts as a store of _____.
fib.explanation: As a store of value, money can be saved now and used later because it keeps its purchasing power over time.

fib.questionText: A deposit account in which money is kept for a fixed period and earns higher interest is called a _____ deposit account.
fib.explanation: A fixed deposit account keeps money locked for an agreed period, earning higher interest because it cannot be withdrawn early.

fib.questionText: When a commercial bank allows a customer to withdraw more than the balance in the account, the facility is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An overdraft allows a current account holder to withdraw beyond the available balance up to an agreed limit, with interest charged.

tf.questionText: Under the barter system, goods were exchanged directly for other goods without using money.
tf.explanation: Barter trade involved exchanging goods directly for other goods, which is why a double coincidence of wants was needed.

tf.questionText: Commercial banks have the power to print and issue a country's banknotes.
tf.explanation: Only the central bank has the authority to print and issue currency; commercial banks deal with deposits, loans and other services.

tf.questionText: One quality of good money is that it should be generally acceptable by people in a society.
tf.explanation: Acceptability is essential because money can only work as a medium of exchange if everyone is willing to accept it.

tf.questionText: A current account usually pays the account holder a high rate of interest.
tf.explanation: A current account is used for frequent payments and usually earns little or no interest, unlike fixed deposit accounts.

tf.questionText: The central bank acts as a banker to the government and to commercial banks.
tf.explanation: The central bank keeps government accounts and also holds reserves for commercial banks, acting as banker to both.

tf.questionText: A major problem of barter trade was the difficulty of storing wealth in perishable goods.
tf.explanation: Goods like food and animals could spoil or die, so storing wealth under barter was difficult, a problem money solved.

tf.questionText: Money used as a measure of value helps people compare the prices of different goods.
tf.explanation: As a measure of value, money gives a common standard for stating prices so that goods can be compared easily.

tf.questionText: A cheque is a form of legal tender that must be accepted as cash everywhere.
tf.explanation: A cheque is only an order to pay and is not legal tender; a seller may refuse to accept it because it can bounce.

tf.questionText: Banking helps trade by keeping traders' money safe and providing loans for business.
tf.explanation: Banks support trade through safekeeping of money, loans, money transfers and convenient means of payment.

tf.questionText: Durability and divisibility are both qualities of good money.
tf.explanation: Good money should be durable so it lasts long and divisible so it can be used for both large and small payments.

summary.correctAnswer: Anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange and for settling debts.
summary.explanation: Money works because society agrees to accept it in trade.

summary.correctAnswer: Medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value, standard of deferred payment.
summary.explanation: These four functions explain why money is useful in trade.

summary.correctAnswer: Acceptability, durability, portability, divisibility, scarcity and stability.
summary.explanation: These qualities make money convenient and reliable for everyday use.

summary.correctAnswer: Direct exchange of goods for goods without using money.
summary.explanation: It was the earliest method of trade before money existed.

summary.correctAnswer: Double coincidence of wants, no common measure of value, difficult to store and divide goods.
summary.explanation: These problems made barter slow and unreliable.

summary.questionText: Main function of a central bank
summary.correctAnswer: Issues currency and controls the money supply of the country.
summary.explanation: It is the top bank that regulates the whole banking system.

summary.questionText: Main function of a commercial bank
summary.correctAnswer: Accepts deposits from the public and gives loans to customers.
summary.explanation: It serves individuals and businesses directly.

summary.correctAnswer: Current account, savings account and fixed deposit account.
summary.explanation: Each account suits a different saving or spending need.

summary.correctAnswer: A written order instructing a bank to pay a stated sum from an account.
summary.explanation: It is a safe and convenient means of payment.

summary.correctAnswer: Safekeeping of money, loans, safe payments and money transfer services.
summary.explanation: Banking makes trade safer, faster and easier to finance.

hoq.questionText: A trader in a rural area receives a large cheque from a customer she does not know well. Why might she still prefer to be paid in cash instead?

options.text: Cash always earns more interest than a cheque
A cheque may bounce if the customer's account has no funds, while cash is final payment
A cheque cannot be written for large amounts
Cash is illegal in rural areas

hoq.explanation: A cheque is only an order to pay and can be dishonoured if the account lacks funds, so cash gives the trader immediate and certain payment.

hoq.questionText: If the central bank wants to reduce the amount of money people can borrow and spend, which action would best help achieve this?

options.text: Lowering interest rates so loans become cheaper
Raising interest rates so borrowing becomes more expensive
Printing more banknotes for the public
Encouraging banks to give more loans

hoq.explanation: By raising interest rates the central bank makes loans more costly, so people borrow and spend less, reducing the money in circulation.

hoq.questionText: Why would a community that uses fast-rotting fish as money face serious problems compared with one that uses metal coins?

options.text: Fish cannot be divided into smaller units
Fish is not durable and loses value quickly, so it is a poor store of value
Metal coins are never accepted in trade
Fish is too heavy to be portable

hoq.explanation: Money should be durable and able to store value; fast-rotting fish decays quickly, so it cannot reliably store wealth the way durable coins can.
